term: cross-world union graph of direct existential support among necessary bearers
definition: A source c precedes a target b if both are de re necessary from w₀ and there is at least one admitted world at which c actually exists and directly supports b. This is a union of explicitly world-indexed direct edges on fixed bearer identities, not a graph of world accessibility, a temporal trace or a transitive closure through contingent beings. Each edge is wholly in its own witness world. A path in the union overlay may combine edges witnessed in different worlds; it is not an actual cross-world causal path or a temporal history.
note: Graph analysis of the #495 possible-world family. A union of individually acyclic world relations can contain a cycle; a necessary-to-necessary restriction can miss contingent intermediate supporters.
